title: Heirloom christening blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm lace christening blanket in 4-ply on 3 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm fine-lace christening blanket in 4-ply (fingering) weight on 3 mm needles. The pattern uses a sixteen-row lace border repeat and a centre diamond mesh. Requires wet blocking over foam to open the lace. About 200 g of 4-ply.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 1st series (1885), §Lace Christening Blanket, gives a 4-ply christening shawl with a diamond-mesh centre and a leaf-vine lace border. The pattern uses yarn-overs, k2tog, and ssk decreases throughout. Mary Thomas's Book of Knitting Patterns (1943), §Christening Blankets, documents similar fine-lace construction.

knitting.gaugeText: 28 sts × 38 rows = 10 × 10 cm in lace pattern on 3 mm needles, blocked. Lace opens significantly with blocking; the unblocked gauge is about 32 sts × 44 rows.

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Halfway check — 211 sts (multiple of 10 + 1 + border), about 45 cm unblocked

glossaryTerms.definition: A lace stitch pattern where yarn-overs and paired decreases (k2tog on the right, ssk on the left) are placed to create diagonal lines that form diamond shapes across the fabric. The repeat is typically 10 stitches wide and 10 rows tall. When blocked, the diamond openwork opens into a regular mesh that is the defining surface of a heirloom lace piece.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 3 mm needles. The centre is
diamond lace mesh
. A sixteen-row leaf-vine border frames all four sides. Finished size: 75 cm wide by 90 cm long when blocked.

This is a long project at fine gauge. The unblocked piece will be noticeably smaller (about 60 × 72 cm) than the blocked dimensions; blocking is not optional and requires a foam mat and T-pins or blocking wires. The challenge level is ADVANCED because the sixteen-row border repeat must be read accurately from a chart at the same time as the centre diamond repeat, and both must be maintained over the full 342-row length. Budget about 200 g (about 800 m / 875 yards) of smooth 4-ply in natural, white, or cream. A single colour shows the lace structure most clearly.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 200 g (about 800 m / 875 yards) of 4-ply (fingering) weight 100% merino or similar smooth single-colour yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3 mm (UK 11 / US 2.5) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Blocking mat
items.qty: Required, lace without blocking is unreadable

items.name: Blocking pins or wires
items.qty: Required for wet blocking to finished dimensions

content.text: Gauge

28 stitches and 38 rows to 10 cm in lace pattern on 3 mm needles, blocked. The unblocked gauge is about 32 stitches and 44 rows. Swatch the full 10-row diamond repeat over at least 20 stitches; wash and block the swatch to its natural lace gauge before calculating the cast-on.

At 28 stitches per 10 cm blocked, 75 cm requires 210 stitches in the centre plus a 10-stitch border on each side. The cast-on is 211 stitches (a multiple of 10 + 1 + 10 border each side = 210 + 1 = 211). If your blocked gauge is 30 per 10 cm, cast on 231 stitches for the same finished width.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on with 4-ply, cast on 211 stitches. Long-tail tail: (3 × 211) / 10 + 15 = 63.3 + 15 = 78.3 cm. Measure 90 cm of tail. At fine gauge, the long-tail cast-on is easier with a smooth needle tip.
Border setup (rows 1 to 16)
Rows 1, 4: k3, p to last 3 sts, k3 on WS; k3, *yo, k4, k2tog, k4; rep from * to last 3 sts, k3 on RS. This introduces the border eyelets.
Centre diamond mesh (repeat 10 sts × 10 rows)
RS row A: k3 border, *k1, yo, ssk, k4, k2tog, yo; rep from * to last 4 sts, k1, k3 border.
RS row B (row 3 of repeat): k3 border, *k2, yo, ssk, k2, k2tog, yo, k1; rep from * to last 4 sts, k2, k3 border.
RS row C (row 5): k3 border, *k3, yo, ssk, k2tog, yo, k2; rep from * to last 4 sts, k3, k3 border.
All WS rows: k3 border, p to last 3 sts, k3 border.

Alternate RS row types within the 10-row repeat to build the diamond lattice. See a diamond-mesh lace chart (any standard 10-stitch diamond repeat in lace references) for the full row sequence. Continue the repeat until the blanket measures 84 cm unblocked (approximately 90 cm blocked).
Stitch count check-ins

At row 171 (about 45 cm unblocked): count across. You should have 211 stitches. Each yo is paired with a decrease on the same RS row; the count should remain constant throughout. At row 341 (about 84 cm unblocked): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Stitch count rising: a yo was placed without a matching decrease on the same row. At fine gauge this is hard to spot in the fabric; check the count after every RS row during the first two repeats.

Diamond pattern turning into diagonal stripes: the row position in the 10-row repeat was lost. Use a row counter or write the row number before setting the work down. Check the yo placement direction matches the chart before you resume.
Yarn splitting on the needle tips: 4-ply yarn frays easily on blunt tips. Use sharp-tipped 3 mm needles (metal or carbon fibre) rather than blunt wooden tips.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with a very relaxed tension, use needles one full size larger (4 mm) for the cast-off row. A tight cast-off edge on lace produces a ridge that cannot be blocked out.
Finishing

Soak the finished piece in cool water for 20 minutes. Gently squeeze out water (do not wring). Pin to measurements on a foam blocking mat: start at the corners, then pin the cast-on and cast-off edges at each repeat point, then the side edges. The piece should be pinned under light tension to open the diamonds. Leave to dry fully, at least 24 hours.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Do not machine wash 4-ply merino lace. Lay flat to dry, reshaping gently. Store flat.
What to try next

From a diamond mesh blanket, try a Shetland-style shawl next. Use the same 4-ply lace. Switch to centre-out construction. The border is knitted sideways and grafted on. The pattern repeat grows to 24 rows.
